risk_description: Baseline simulation conservatism partially mitigated by gamma anchor bug fix (2026-03-22). The prior pooled mean gap (3.07% sim vs 18.05% hist) was resolved in a prior rebuild (pooled bias 20.25% vs 18.87% hist). A second bug was then found: gamma_long_run_nominal_pp used price_growth (Δ log real_price) instead of Δ log nominal_house_price, producing near-zero anchors for flat-real-return regions. Bug fixed 2026-03-22 in canonical_rebuild.py. Target regions improved: West Midlands −17pp→−11pp, Wales −9pp→−3pp, Yorkshire −10pp→−6pp. Remaining negative bias in West Midlands, Wales, Yorkshire is smaller but unresolved. Several regions now show positive bias; Northern Ireland remains high (+19pp) due to sigma cap (see R026). Overall pooled bias is acceptable but regional dispersion is wide.
mitigation_needed: Gamma anchor bug fixed 2026-03-22. Remaining bias driven by sigma cap (R026) and valuation-gap closure assumptions. Monitor after next panel rebuild and reconsider regional sigma cap when more data available.

risk_description: Rate channel sign is fixed but magnitude remains unstable across subsamples. Approach B (stability-test-only, no spec change) implemented 2026-03-23. Stability diagnostic: per-region OLS on full/early(2005–2015)/late(2015–) subsamples with HAC maxlags=24. Threshold 5.0 (not 3.0): at 3.0, all 12 regions flag because early-period (2005-2015 ZLB era) rate variation was near-zero, making early betas imprecisely estimated and often reverse-signed — the ratio measures identification noise, not structural break. At 5.0, 5 regions flagged (North East 5.99, Scotland 6.91, South West 12.03, Wales 6.19, Yorkshire 5.64). All flagged regions have early-period |t| < 2 (ZLB identification failure). Full-sample beta is the appropriate pooled estimate for annual-frequency use. test_rate_channel_stability added to test suite. HAC maxlags raised from 12 to 24 to better absorb UK rate-cycle persistence (3–5 year cycles).
mitigation_needed: Approach B implemented 2026-03-23: stability test only (no spec change), threshold 5.0, HAC maxlags=24. Five regions flagged as monitored-open (R010). Full-sample beta used for all production scoring. See regional_rate_stability.csv.

risk_description: Wales 5-year simulated IQR is severely compressed relative to historical. Diagnostic (2026-03-22): kappa=0.255, sigma=0.025 (at global floor; heuristic=0.044), sim p25/p75=13.11/18.40pp (IQR_sim=5.29pp), hist p25/p75=3.90/30.05pp (IQR_hist=26.15pp), ratio=0.202 (20.2% of historical). Root cause: sigma is at the global floor (0.025) and the low kappa dampens OU path spread. Required sigma_floor to bring IQR within 20% of historical is 0.115 — far exceeding the 0.035 override threshold defined in the recalibration protocol. Override not implemented. IQR compression reflects genuine calibration difficulty when sigma_heuristic < 0.05 and kappa < 0.30.
mitigation_needed: IQR prior implemented 2026-03-31 in canonical_rebuild.py. Sigma raised iteratively to target sim IQR >= 35% of historical. Wales: sigma 0.02500 → 0.04429, IQR ratio 0.203 → 0.359 (hist_IQR=22.45pp, sim_IQR_new=8.06pp). Yorkshire: sigma 0.05500 → 0.05500 (no change required — ratio already 0.443 >= 0.35). Remaining compression documented. Full recalibration scheduled 2026-06-30.

risk_description: Yorkshire and The Humber 5-year simulated IQR is compressed relative to historical. Root cause: calibrated sigma at 0.055 is insufficient to reproduce the historical IQR at this kappa level. risk_description: Consumer and REIT scenario weights use different mechanisms — consumer_weights are hardcoded in canonical_rebuild.py with a deliberate downside-skewed prior (adverse scenarios weighted 0.45 combined); reit_weights are computed dynamically as equal-weight 1/N from config.ui.scenario_labels at runtime. Adding or renaming a scenario silently changes REIT weighting but not consumer weighting. These should use the same mechanism. RESOLVED 2026-03-22: both weight sets migrated to config/parameters.json under scoring.scenario_consumer_weights and scoring.scenario_reit_weights. canonical_rebuild.py reads both from config. engine.py validates app_consumer_weights and app_reit_weights sum to 1.0 at module load. test_weight_consistency confirms no hardcoded dicts remain.

risk_description: 5 of 12 regions are at the annual sigma cap (0.120): East Midlands, East of England, London, North East, North West. Northern Ireland (sigma=0.120) also hit the cap but was separately tested. SIGMA CAP TEST (2026-03-22): per-region sigma_cap_overrides infrastructure implemented in config.py + canonical_rebuild.py. Northern Ireland tested at cap=0.150 (sigma→0.150, median=42.30pp) and cap=0.135 (sigma→0.135, median=42.34pp). Original cap=0.120: median=42.38pp. Median is insensitive to sigma cap (range <0.1pp across three caps), CONFIRMING the +19pp gap (sim 42.38 vs hist_p50 23.18) is driven by gamma (2.39%/yr) and kappa (0.841/yr) producing fast reversion to a richly-valued fair-value equilibrium, NOT by sigma cap. CORRECTION to original R026 diagnosis: sigma cap does NOT inflate medians; it affects IQR only. Sigma_cap_override for NI reverted to global 0.120. Infrastructure (sigma_cap_overrides in config/canonical_rebuild.py) retained for future use.
mitigation_needed: Northern Ireland +19pp median gap requires investigation of the fair-value equilibrium (mu=235k vs current 196k = -16.7% gap) and gamma drift. The OU process with kappa=0.841 closes 98.5% of the -16.7% gap in 5 years, driving the high simulated median. This is model behaviour given the inputs, not a numerical error. To reduce the gap: revisit the mu_equilibrium estimate for Northern Ireland or cap the gap-closure contribution in the baseline scenario. Sigma cap test infrastructure available for future use.
